_meta.note: roles on every entry below are sourced from ssot-equip-slots.md SS2.3-SS2.5 (Lane I2's own SSOT, dated the same day as ssot-affixes.md), not from a naive id-translation of ssot-affixes.md SS4.3's stale 12-role matrix. See atom.shield-capacity's notes for the full reasoning; every other entry in this file inherits the same sourcing unless its own notes say otherwise.

entries.name: Shield Capacity
entries.notes: SHIPPED — id kept verbatim per naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies g.shield-stat.existingFamilies. `roles` deliberately DIVERGES from the pattern the g.on-hit and g.elem-power partitions used (a straight id-translation of ssot-affixes.md SS4.3's old 12-role matrix): that matrix predates `ward-array`, which ssot-equip-slots.md SS2.4 states was carved out of `core-guard`/`mantle`/`head-guard`/`girdle` SPECIFICALLY to give the four shield families (named by name) their own budget — 'folding shields into core-guard would put two unrelated survivability currencies in one budget.' Reading the old matrix's nonzero cells for those four roles as still-additive would re-introduce exactly the overlap the new role was created to remove, so this file omits them. `armament-secondary` stays legal: ssot-equip-slots.md's own worked example (SS7, 'off-hand') rolls `shield_capacity.fire` on it. `jewel-major` stays legal on the older, uncontradicted rationale that it is 'the only role legal for everything' (ssot-affixes.md SS4.3 commentary). `jewel-minor-a`/`-b` are excluded on an explicit, specific, same-day rule (ssot-equip-slots.md SS2.5, point 3): 'the six strongest families -- bulwark, savagery, and the four shield families -- are absent from the minor-jewel family list on every frame.' That sentence names this group by name and postdates the old matrix's undifferentiated jewel-minor=1 cell. `element` is a channel variant, not a params key, matching the exemplar's `elemental_power` pattern exactly (35-row expansion, not 5). RUNTIME HONESTY: `stat.derived` is quarantined None/None/None (D6, classes.v1.json) — nothing binds this row to gear yet. This is distinct from the shield RUNTIME itself: shield-system-spec.md is implemented and `ShieldRuntime` already reads `combat.shield.capacity.*` at the grant barrier (SS2.6); what is missing is the item-affix path (BattleStatComposer, E12) that would let an equipped item populate that channel. Author now; nothing binds until then.

entries.name: Shield Toughness
entries.displayTemplate: {element} shields take {value} less damage per hit
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. Same `roles` sourcing as `atom.shield-capacity` — ssot-equip-slots.md SS2.4 names `shield_toughness` explicitly in ward-array's family list. `toughness` is the owner-side term in ShieldMath's `breakerDelta = pen - toughness` (shield-system-spec.md SS2.4); it lowers the damage a hit deals to the pool, so the display template reads as a reduction rather than a gain, unlike the additive-power exemplar pattern.

entries.name: Shield Regeneration
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. Same `roles` sourcing as `atom.shield-capacity`. `powerBand: low` against the sibling pair's `medium`: shield-system-spec.md SS2.6 reads this channel as a continuous HP-per-second trickle (front-shield rule, no multi-dip across stacked shields), which is a smaller per-tick pull than a flat capacity or per-hit toughness number — the same relative-pull judgement the exemplar makes between its own two sibling entries.

entries.name: Shield Penetration
entries.notes: SHIPPED, id kept verbatim. The one ATTACKER-side family in this group (shield-system-spec.md SS2.3: pen is read off the hitter, toughness/capacity/regen off the shield's owner) — this is the lane note's point that g.shield-stat is 'the shield stat surface', not 'shield defence'. `roles` is deliberately the narrowest in the file: ssot-equip-slots.md SS2.3 names `shield_pen` in `armament-primary`'s own role description ('raw attack, elemental power, shield penetration' -- the identity slot), and `ward-array` ('the depleting outer layer... everything that is spent before HP') is an owner-side concept that does not fit an attacker stat, so it is excluded here even though it carries the other three families. `jewel-major` kept on the same generic-slot rationale as the other three entries.

entries.name: Shield Surge
entries.notes: NEW family minted on this group's reserved `shld` stem (naming.v1.json idNamespaces.affixFamilies), word `surge` -- short and mechanical, describing the swell in the pool rather than a flavour concept. Same channel as `atom.shield-capacity`, different `op`: `Flat` adds shield hit points, `Increased` scales them, and they compose the way `elemental_power`/`elpw-amplify` compose on the prefix side (the exemplar's own worked pair). `roles` copies `atom.shield-capacity`'s exactly, since the two are the same channel at different ops and the role legality question is 'can this slot touch shield capacity at all', not 'which op'. `powerBand: low` against the Flat sibling's `medium` is the deliberate secondary-pull judgement the exemplar's `elpw-amplify` entry makes for the same reason.

entries.name: Shield Cycling
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `shld`, word `cycle` -- the regen tick repeating faster, a mechanical description of the front-shield-rule trickle (shield-system-spec.md SS2.6), not a flavour word. The `Increased` sibling of `atom.shield-regen`, same channel, same `roles` copy-down rationale as `atom.shld-surge`. `powerBand: low`, matching its own Flat sibling's already-`low` band rather than sitting a full rung under it -- the regen pair is the one place in this file where both op-siblings share a band, because the Flat family was already the smallest pull in the group (see `atom.shield-regen`'s own notes) and a further step down would fall through the tier-1 legibility floor (bands.v1.json tierScaling.overlap.knownEdgeCase).

entries.name: Shield Breach
entries.notes: NEW family, stem `shld`, word `breach`. The `Increased` sibling of `atom.shield-pen`, inheriting its narrower `roles` list (armament-primary, jewel-major) unchanged -- an attacker stat scales the same way whether it adds or multiplies. This is the third and last of the three `Increased` siblings minted in this partition; `atom.shield-toughness` deliberately does NOT get one (would bring the group to 8 families against a ~7 target, and a percentage multiplier on an already-subtractive per-hit reduction is the least intuitive of the four candidates -- the odd one out is the flat mitigation stat, not one of the three that read naturally as 'more of this resource/attack').
